title: American Tourister
about: Luggage brand founded in Providence in 1933
blurb: Luggage first made by the brothers Sol and Irving Koffler in Providence, Rhode Island, in 1933, and part of Samsonite since the 1990s.

title: Baggu
about: American brand of bags made from recycled materials
blurb: Casual bags at a low price, made with recycled materials, and best known for its reusable shopping bags of ripstop nylon.

title: Bandolier bag
blurb: A Native American shoulder pouch on a broad strap. From the fur-trade era on it was sewn from wool broadcloth, lined with calico, edged with silk ribbon and often beaded all over.

title: Bayong
blurb: A bayong is a type of bag from the Philippines made by weaving dried leaves, usually from buri in the Visayas and pandan in Luzon. It is also made using native Philippine plants such as abaca, bacbac, karagumoy, sabutan, romblon and tikog.

title: Bindle
blurb: A bundle tied to the end of a stick and carried over the shoulder, the luggage of storybook wanderers.

title: Birkin bag
blurb: Hermès's hand-stitched leather tote, sketched on an aeroplane sick bag for Jane Birkin in 1984.

title: Bota bag
blurb: A bota bag is a traditional Spanish liquid receptacle, used mainly as a wineskin. It is often made out of leather, and is typically used to carry wine, although any liquid can be filled into it.

title: Cambridge Satchel Company
about: Leather satchel maker from Cambridge, England
blurb: Founded in 2008 by Julie Deane and her mother Freda Thomas to pay school fees, it makes colourful leather satchels based on the old Oxford and Cambridge school satchel.

title: Chanel 2.55
blurb: The Chanel 2.55 is a luxury leather handbag or purse designed by Coco Chanel and manufactured by the fashion house of Chanel.

title: Coach New York
blurb: Coach New York, commonly known as Coach, is an American fashion house headquartered in New York City specializing in handbags, luggage, and accessories, as well as ready-to-wear. Coach licenses its name and branding to Luxottica for eyewear, and Paris-based Interparfums for fragrances.

title: Coin purse
about: Small pouch made for carrying coins
blurb: A purse or pouch, sometimes called coin purse for clarity, is a small money bag or pouch, made for carrying coins. In most Commonwealth countries it is known simply as a purse, while "purse" in the United States usually refers to a handbag. An obsolete variant is a porte-monnaie.

title: Creel
about: Wicker basket used for carrying fish or blocks of peat
blurb: A creel is a wicker basket usually used for carrying fish or blocks of peat. It is also a fish trap used to catch lobsters and other crustaceans. In modern times, the term has come to encompass various types of wicker baskets used by anglers or commercial fishermen to hold fish or other prey.

title: Dillybag
blurb: A dillybag or dilly bag, also known as a mindirr or bulbbe, among other names, is a traditional Australian Aboriginal bag generally woven from plant fibres. Dillybags are mainly designed and used by women to gather and transport food, and are most commonly found in the northern parts of Australia.

title: Dior Saddle bag
blurb: The Dior Saddle bag is a designer handbag introduced in 1999 by French fashion house Dior under the creative direction of John Galliano.

title: Dooney & Bourke
about: Leather goods brand from Norwalk, Connecticut
blurb: Founded in Norwalk, Connecticut, in 1975 to make belts, braces and ties for men, and now known for its handbags.

title: Eastpak
blurb: The backpack maker that began in Boston in 1952 as Eastern Canvas Products and took the name Eastpak in 1976.

title: Fendi Baguette
about: Small Fendi handbag first made in 1997
blurb: The small Fendi shoulder bag of 1997, often called the first It bag. Fendi has since made it in hundreds of designs and sold more than a million.

title: Filson
blurb: Founded in Seattle in 1897 to outfit prospectors heading north for the Klondike Gold Rush, Filson still makes rugged bags, luggage and outdoor clothing.

title: Fjällräven Kånken
blurb: Kånken is a backpack sold by the Swedish outdoor equipment company Fjällräven. It is Fjällräven's best-known and best-selling product.

title: Footlocker
blurb: A footlocker is a small trunk to be placed at the foot of a bed, used to store personal belongings. They can be secured by a padlock or combination lock, and are often used by soldiers or other military personnel.

title: Frost River
about: Waxed canvas packs from Duluth, Minnesota
blurb: Waxed canvas luggage, canoe packs and business bags, each cut, sewn, riveted and finished in Duluth, Minnesota, and guaranteed for life.

title: Furoshiki
blurb: A square Japanese wrapping cloth that knots into a bag for gifts, lunches or bottles.

title: Gaji bag
blurb: A gaji bag is a large, typically unfastened bag with parallel handles that emerge from the sides of its pouch. They are often used as reusable shopping bags. Gaji bags originated from the rural village of Jingliao in the Houbi District of Tainan, Taiwan during the Japanese colonial period.

title: Globe-Trotter
blurb: Luxury suitcases made by hand in a Hertfordshire factory by a company founded in 1897.

title: Goyard
blurb: A Paris trunk maker since 1853 and in the Goyard family's hands since the 19th century, known for luggage and totes in its chevron-patterned canvas.

title: Hebao
blurb: Hebao, sometimes referred as Propitious pouch in English, is a generic term used to refer to Chinese embroidery pouches, purses, or small bags. When they are used as Chinese perfume pouch, they are referred to as Xiāngnáng, Xiāngbāo, or Xiāngdài. In everyday life, hebao are used to store items.

title: Hidesign
blurb: Leather bags, wallets and belts from a company based in Pondicherry, which has grown from India to operations in some two dozen countries.

title: Hobo bag
blurb: The hobo bag is a style of handbag or purse that is typically large and characterized by a crescent shape, a slouchy posture and a long strap designed to wear over the shoulder. Hobo bags are made out of soft, flexible materials and tend to slump, or slouch, when set down.

title: JanSport
blurb: JanSport is an American brand of backpacks and collegiate apparel, now owned by VF Corporation, one of the world's largest apparel companies. JanSport is the world's largest backpack maker.

title: Kate Spade New York
about: Fashion house founded in New York in 1993
blurb: Founded in 1993 by Kate and Andy Spade with Elyce Arons and Pamela Bell, the label began with handbags and is now part of Tapestry, the owner of Coach.

title: Kelly bag
blurb: The trapezoid Hermès handbag renamed after Grace Kelly used hers to shield herself from photographers.

title: Kinchaku
blurb: Kinchaku is a traditional Japanese drawstring bag, used like a handbag for carrying around personal possessions; smaller ones are usually used as sagemono, and used to carry small objects such as loose coinage, cosmetics, lucky charms, hand warmers and mobile phones.

title: Lady Dior
about: Dior handbag named for Diana, Princess of Wales
blurb: A Dior handbag designed by Gianfranco Ferré in 1994, first called Chouchou and later renamed in honour of Diana, Princess of Wales.

title: Moynat
blurb: A Paris trunk maker founded in 1849 by Octavie and François Coulembier with the travel-goods specialist Pauline Moynat; its trunks were shown at the World's Fairs.

title: Nantucket lightship basket
about: Rattan and wood basket from Nantucket Island
blurb: First woven by lightship crews off Nantucket in the 19th century: rattan worked over a mould, an odd number of wooden staves, a solid wooden base and a nailed, lashed rim.

title: Pannier
about: One of a pair of baskets, bags, boxes, or similar containers
blurb: A pannier /ˈpæniər/ is a basket, bag, box, or similar container, carried in pairs either slung over the back of a beast of burden, or attached to the sides of a bicycle or motorcycle. The term derives from a Middle English borrowing of the Old French panier, meaning "bread basket".

title: Parfleche
blurb: A parfleche is a Native American rawhide container that is embellished by painting, incising, or both. Envelope-shaped parfleches have historically been used to contain items such as household tools or foods, such as dried meat or pemmican. They were commonly made in pairs and hung from saddles.

title: Peg and Awl
about: Waxed canvas and reclaimed goods from Philadelphia
blurb: Started in 2010 in a Philadelphia row home, Peg and Awl hand-makes waxed canvas bags, reclaimed-wood home goods and journals from abandoned materials.

title: Picnic basket
about: Covered basket for carrying food and utensils
blurb: A picnic basket or picnic hamper is a basket intended to hold food and tableware for a picnic meal. Picnic baskets are standard equipment at many picnics. A traditional picnic hamper is made of woven wicker.

title: Red-white-blue bag
about: Nylon carry bag associated with Hong Kong culture
blurb: Red-white-blue bag or laundry bag is a carriage bag made out of nylon canvas in colors of red, white and blue. It originated in Hong Kong in the 1960s and has become a representative of Hong Kong culture.

title: Reticule
about: Small handbag, originally with a drawstring closure, and often decorated with beadwork
blurb: A reticule, also known as a ridicule or indispensable, was a type of small handbag or purse, similar to a modern evening bag, used mainly from 1795 to 1820. The reticule became popular with the advent of Regency fashions in the late 18th century.

title: Rimowa
about: Luggage maker from Cologne, founded in 1898
blurb: A Cologne luggage maker since 1898, whose aluminium suitcases with parallel grooves are recognisable on any baggage carousel.

title: Sabretache
blurb: A sabretache is a flat bag or pouch, which was worn suspended from the belt of a cavalry soldier together with the sabre.

title: Saddlebag
blurb: Saddlebags are bags that are attached to saddles.

title: Samsonite
blurb: Samsonite International S.A. is a Luxembourg-based multinational luggage manufacturer and retailer, with products ranging from large suitcases to small toiletries, bags and briefcases. The company was founded in 1910 in Denver, Colorado, United States.

title: Santiniketan Leather Goods
about: Leather products from a region of India
blurb: Santiniketan Leather Goods are leather products made in Santiniketan and surrounding villages near Kolkata, West Bengal, India. The material used is vegetable tanned leather with art work done by touch dyeing.

title: Showbag
about: Themed bag of items often sold at Australian agricultural shows
blurb: A showbag is a themed bag of commercial products, novelty items and promotional merchandise, usually made available for purchase. It is a distinctive feature of Australian agricultural shows, where they are sold from stalls; they can also be found at exhibitions, festivals and fundraising events.

title: Steamer trunk
blurb: A large travel chest from the age of ocean liners, plastered with hotel labels.

title: Tom Bihn
about: Bags designed and made in Seattle
blurb: Since 1972 Tom Bihn has designed and manufactured durable bags, from backpacks and travel bags to totes, with a factory showroom in Seattle.

title: Tumi Inc.
blurb: Tumi Holdings, Inc., is a manufacturer of high-end suitcases and bags for travel based in Edison, New Jersey. It was a unit of Doughty Hanson & Co. from 2004 until after its 2012 initial public offering, which preceded its acquisition by Samsonite in 2016.

title: Vera Bradley
about: American luggage and handbag design company
blurb: Vera Bradley Sales, LLC is an American travel gear design company, founded by Barbara Bradley Baekgaard and Patricia R. Miller in 1982. As of 2026, its home office is in Roanoke, Indiana. The company was named after Baekgaard's mother.

title: VIP Industries
blurb: The Mumbai company behind the suitcases of generations of Indian travellers, and now one of the largest luggage makers in the world. It also makes Skybags.

title: Zouk
blurb: Handcrafted, cruelty-free and proudly Indian bags, wallets and luggage; the idea came to its founder on a visit to the white desert of Kutch.
